title: Learning to Code at Thirty-Two
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Two years ago, I was working as a cashier, and although the job paid the bills, I felt like I was standing still while everyone around me was moving forward.
Narrator: [honestly] I had always been curious about computers, but I never believed someone like me, without a technical background, could actually learn to code.
Narrator: [reflective] Then a coworker mentioned a free online course, so I decided to try it, mostly because I had nothing to lose.
Narrator: [determined] I studied for one hour every night after my shift, even when I was exhausted and wanted nothing more than to sleep.
Narrator: [honestly] The first few weeks were confusing, because the instructions used words I had never heard before, and I often felt completely lost.
Narrator: [gently] I almost quit during the third week, when a simple exercise took me four hours instead of the thirty minutes it was supposed to take.
Narrator: [warmly] But then I finished my first small project, a simple calculator, and something inside me shifted completely.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I realized that although I was slow, I was still learning, and that mattered more than speed.
Narrator: [reflective] So I kept going, week after week, even when progress felt painfully small some nights.
Narrator: [with feeling] Six months later, I built a small website for my cousin's bakery, and she actually used it to take orders.
Narrator: [warmly] That moment felt bigger than any exam I ever passed in school, because I had built it completely from nothing.
Narrator: [determined] Because of that project, I applied for an entry-level position at a small software company, even though I doubted I was ready.
Narrator: [with a small smile] I got the job last month, and although I still have so much to learn, I finally believe I belong in that world.
Narrator: [peacefully] Whenever a new concept feels impossible now, I remember that calculator, and I remind myself that confusion is simply the beginning of understanding.
Narrator: [warmly] I still work slower than colleagues who studied this in university, but I no longer feel embarrassed about the path that brought me here.
